image_description: A white minibus (likely a Fiat Ducato or similar model) parked on a paved surface. The vehicle is shown from a front-three-quarter angle, displaying the driver's side. It features a high roof, a row of tinted passenger windows, a sliding door track, and standard steel wheels. There is a blue logo/text on the front hood and a small blue square sticker on the rear side panel. The background includes a corrugated metal wall and some greenery.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Boxy body shape noticeably shorter than a full-size bus, yet tall enough for passengers to stand or sit upright comfortably.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The vehicle exhibits the characteristic high-roof van silhouette, distinct from low-profile cars and significantly shorter than full-size transit buses.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Large windshield and row of side windows along passenger area.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A large, single-piece windshield is visible, along with a clear sequence of side windows extending back from the driver's cabin.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Height is substantial, with entrance door at front or mid-body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The vehicle height is consistent with a minibus. A vertical seam and handle indicating a sliding entrance door are visible behind the front wheel arch.
The vertical cut line and the horizontal rail/track detail above the window line confirm the presence of a sliding door mechanism.
The short nose and hood structure ahead of the windshield indicate a front-engine layout typical of this class of vehicle.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rear flat or slightly angled panel with taillights and license plate mount.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is cropped at the rear wheel; the rear bumper, taillights, and back panel are outside the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: White, yellow, or company livery paint with route markings.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The vehicle is painted white with black trim. There is blue text/logo on the hood, fitting the description of company livery.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Standard van-sized wheels with steel or alloy rims.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible front wheel is a standard steel rim with hubcap, proportional to the vehicle body.
The length and window configuration suggest a capacity within the 4-10 passenger range, consistent with the minibus definition.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The blue script on the front hood is illegible and lacks coherent character structure, appearing as AI-generated pseudo-text rather than a real brand logo.
The side mirror housing appears slightly fused with the door frame, lacking a sharp separation gap. The door handle geometry is somewhat soft and indistinct.
The shadow under the front tire is weak, and the tire's contact with the ground feels slightly 'floaty' rather than firmly grounded, though not structurally broken.

selected_experts.reason: To verify the specific make/model consistency and ensure it falls correctly within the 'minibus' taxonomy rather than a standard van or full-size bus.
To check for structural coherence between the wheels and the body, and to ensure the background wall does not bleed into the vehicle edges.
To audit the sharpness of the window frames and the sliding door tracks, which are common failure points for fusion artifacts in vehicle generation.
To specifically analyze the illegible blue text on the hood and the blue square on the side to confirm if they are gibberish or distorted real text.

focus_areas: Legibility and structure of the blue text/logo on the hood.
Structural integrity of the sliding door track and handle.
Grounding of the tires and shadow consistency.
Sharpness of the window pillars and mirror assembly.
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'text_gibberish' artifact on the hood. While the vehicle structure is strong, AI models often fail at rendering coherent logos. Verify if the text auditor confirms this as non-readable gibberish. Also, check if the geometric depth auditor finds any subtle warping in the straight lines of the corrugated background wall, which can indicate global perspective errors.
